extracted.intended_audience: press officers, principal investigators, communications staff preparing press releases or other dissemination materials for NIH-funded research
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and coordinating press releases and other public-facing dissemination for research supported by NIH awards, including required acknowledgments, coordination steps, and quality/content recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Acknowledgment Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each publication, press release, or other document about research supported by an NIH award must include an acknowledgment of NIH award support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledgment must appear on any public-facing material describing NIH-supported research; see required elements for specifics (institute/center name and grant number).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notify NIH communications offices before issuing
rubrics_metrics.description: Notify NIH communications offices prior to issuing press releases or other dissemination about NIH-supported research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advance notification enables coordination, potential highlighting on NIH websites, and allows NIH PIOs to prepare or respond; use provided NIH Communications Office contacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: May highlight release on NIH websites
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH may highlight your press release on NIH websites as part of coordination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notify NIH early if you want consideration for site highlighting; coordination increases visibility and alignment with NIH messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate with funding institute/center (IC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinate the release with the funding institute/center (IC) that supported the research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work with the relevant IC PIO/science writer to ensure IC-specific style, messaging, and timing are aligned; ICs may require their own review or style adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow advance review by NIH
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide NIH an opportunity for advance review of press materials prior to public release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advance review is part of the coordination process so NIH can verify acknowledgment, accuracy, and appropriate disclaimers; timing expectations should be clarified with the IC/PIO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required element: NIH institute/center name
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases must include the NIH institute/center name that provided support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spell out the full name of the supporting NIH institute or center (IC) in the acknowledgment section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required element: Grant number
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases must include the grant number associated with the NIH award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the full grant number(s) for the NIH award(s) that supported the research; this is required for tracking and compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required element: Specific disclaimer language
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the required NIH disclaimer in materials: "The content is solely the responsibility of the authors and does not necessarily represent the official views of the National Institutes of Health."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the exact disclaimer wording provided by NIH; place it in the acknowledgment or disclaimer section of the release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mention NIH early in press release text
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategic recommendation to mention NIH early in the press release text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Placing the NIH acknowledgment or mention early helps signal funding and credibility to readers; balance this with lead messaging about findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider including a quote from an NIH expert
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider including a quote from an NIH expert to provide outside perspective on significance and add credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If appropriate, coordinate with NIH to identify an expert or use IC/PIO-approved quotes; ensure accuracy and conflict-of-interest considerations are managed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact NIH Communications Office for coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: Use NIH Communications Office contacts to coordinate dissemination (e.g., Craig Fritz: 301-402-4507, fritzcm@mail.nih.gov).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NIH Communications Office works across 27 ICs and coordinates with PIOs and science writers; use these contacts for cross-IC coordination and questions about policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider innovative dissemination methods beyond traditional press releases
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH recommends considering nonspecialist summaries, blog posts, visual abstracts, video abstracts, infographics, podcasts, social media campaigns, and plain language summaries as dissemination channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select formats appropriate to the audience and message; visual and plain-language products can increase reach and comprehension among nonexpert audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge NIH support (implicit rubric item 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: A press release for NIH-funded research should acknowledge NIH support (institute + grant number).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 'Required elements' for exact expectations and language; acknowledgment is mandatory for NIH-funded work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include required disclaimer (implicit rubric item 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the NIH-required disclaimer in the press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the exact NIH disclaimer phrase; ensure it is visible and correctly worded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate with NIH PIO before release (implicit rubric item 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinate press release content and timing with the NIH Public Information Officer (PIO) prior to issuing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordination allows for institutional review, ensures compliance with IC-specific requirements, and can facilitate amplification via NIH channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite peer-reviewed publication (DOI) (implicit rubric item 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite the underlying peer-reviewed publication and include its DOI in the release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing a DOI enables reporters and readers to access the full study; avoid overselling preliminary or non–peer-reviewed findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use plain language for general audience (implicit rubric item 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Write the release in plain language suitable for a general audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid jargon, explain technical terms, and focus on clear takeaways; consider readability targets and editing for nonexpert comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider health literacy (Grade 8 reading) (implicit rubric item 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim for health literacy standards, roughly a Grade 8 reading level, when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use short sentences, common words, and clear organization; employ plain-language summaries to meet health literacy goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish findings from speculation (implicit rubric item 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly distinguish between study findings, interpretations, and speculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overstating implications, emphasize limitations, and explicitly state when conclusions are tentative or require further research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include researcher contact (implicit rubric item 8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide contact information for the researcher(s) involved in the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include phone/email for media follow-up and clarify availability; coordinate with institutional communications offices if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include NIH expert quote where appropriate (implicit rubric item 9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a quote from an NIH expert where appropriate to provide context and credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate any NIH quotes with the relevant IC and PIO to ensure appropriateness and approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include multimedia (researcher photos, lab images) (implicit rubric item 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide supporting multimedia such as researcher photos or lab images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-quality visuals can aid media coverage and public engagement; ensure permissions and image captions are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide visual/video abstracts when available (implicit rubric item 11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer visual abstracts or video abstracts to supplement the textual release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These can improve accessibility and shareability on social platforms; ensure they accurately represent the findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be honest about clinical applicability (implicit rubric item 12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly communicate the clinical applicability (or lack thereof) of the research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid implying immediate clinical relevance when results are preclinical or early-stage; state translational steps required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note study design (RCT, observational, animal) (implicit rubric item 13)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify the study design (e.g., randomized controlled trial, observational study, animal research).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifying the design helps audiences and reporters assess strength of evidence; include key methodological details without excessive jargon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include confidence intervals (implicit rubric item 14)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include confidence intervals when reporting quantitative results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide measures of uncertainty rather than only p-values; present results in a way that nontechnical audiences can understand (with explanation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Report effect sizes in absolute terms (implicit rubric item 15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report effect sizes using absolute terms (not only relative terms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absolute risk differences and counts are often more interpretable for the public than relative percentages; show both if helpful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be available for follow-up (researcher + PIO) (implicit rubric item 16)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure both the researcher and the PIO are available for media follow-up after release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear contact availability windows and designate spokespeople; rapid follow-up improves accurate coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate with appropriate ICs and use IC-specific style
rubrics_metrics.description: For topic-specific research, coordinate with the relevant IC (e.g., NCI, NIMH, NIA, NIAID) and follow any IC-specific style or instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different NIH institutes and centers may have preferred language, review processes, or amplification channels—engage the correct IC PIO early in planning.
